gaps.sentence: They've postponed ___ the new bridge until spring.

gaps.explanation: Negative infinitive: promised not to be late — 'not' goes before 'to'.

gaps.sentence: They're planning ___ the flat before selling it.
gaps.explanation: plan + to-infinitive (plan on + -ing also occurs informally): planning to redecorate.

gaps.sentence: We can't risk ___ the connection flight.
I really can't afford ___ on holiday this year.
gaps.explanation: afford takes the to-infinitive: can't afford to go.

gaps.sentence: They agreed ___ the deadline by a week.
gaps.explanation: 'Agree to do something' takes the to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: He apologized for ___ so abrupt in the meeting.
There's no point ___ about it now.
gaps.explanation: there's no point + -ing: no point worrying.
